subject: PLB
body: A 64-year-old man has 40 minutes of central crushing chest pain. ECG shows ST elevation in II, III and aVF. Which coronary artery is most likely occluded?
explanation: Inferior leads (II, III, aVF) usually reflect the right coronary artery.

subject: PLB
body: A 58-year-old woman with STEMI presents within 90 minutes of symptom onset to a hospital with a cath lab. What is the definitive treatment?
explanation: Primary PCI is preferred if it can be delivered within 120 minutes of when fibrinolysis could have been given.

subject: PLB
body: A 70-year-old man has new atrial fibrillation. CHA₂DS₂-VASc is 3. He has no bleeding history. What is the most appropriate long-term management to reduce stroke risk?
options: A direct oral anticoagulant such as apixaban
explanation: Offer anticoagulation (DOAC first line) when CHA₂DS₂-VASc ≥2; aspirin alone is not recommended for stroke prevention in AF.

subject: PLB
body: A 55-year-old Black African man has clinic blood pressure 162/98 confirmed by ambulatory monitoring. He is not diabetic. What is the first-line drug?
options: An ACE inhibitor such as ramipril
A calcium-channel blocker such as amlodipine
explanation: UK guidance: for people of Black African or African-Caribbean origin without diabetes, start with a CCB (or an ARB in preference to an ACE inhibitor if a RAS blocker is chosen).

subject: PLB
body: A 45-year-old white woman without diabetes is diagnosed with stage 2 hypertension. What is the first-line drug?
options: An ACE inhibitor such as ramipril
explanation: Under 55 and not of Black African or African-Caribbean origin: ACE inhibitor or ARB first.

subject: PLB
body: A 30-year-old man has sharp chest pain relieved by sitting forward. ECG shows widespread saddle-shaped ST elevation and PR depression. What is the diagnosis?
explanation: Pleuritic pain eased by leaning forward with widespread concave ST elevation is classic for pericarditis.

subject: PLB
body: A 72-year-old man has sudden tearing chest pain radiating to the back. Blood pressure differs by 30 mmHg between arms. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Tearing pain to the back with inter-arm BP difference suggests dissection; arrange urgent CT angiography.

subject: PLB
body: A 78-year-old woman has exertional syncope and an ejection systolic murmur radiating to the carotids. What is the most likely valve lesion?
explanation: Angina, syncope and heart failure with an ejection systolic murmur radiating to the carotids.

subject: PLB
body: Which drug class has been shown to reduce mortality in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction and should be started alongside an ACE inhibitor?
options: A beta-blocker licensed for heart failure, such as bisoprolol
explanation: ACE inhibitor + beta-blocker are first-line; loop diuretics relieve symptoms but do not improve survival.

subject: PLB
body: A patient with a broad-complex tachycardia at 180 bpm is hypotensive and confused. What is the immediate management?
explanation: Adverse features (shock, syncope, ischaemia, heart failure) mean synchronised cardioversion.

subject: PLB
body: A stable patient has a regular narrow-complex tachycardia at 190 bpm. Vagal manoeuvres fail. What is next?
explanation: Adenosine 6 mg, then 12 mg, then further 12 mg if needed, with ECG monitoring.

subject: PLB
body: A 68-year-old with pneumonia is confused, urea 8 mmol/L, respiratory rate 32/min, BP 100/58 mmHg. What is the CURB-65 score?
explanation: Confusion 1, urea >7 1, RR ≥30 1, SBP <90 or DBP ≤60 1, age ≥65 1 = 5.

subject: PLB
body: A tall 21-year-old man has sudden pleuritic chest pain and breathlessness. The chest X-ray shows a 3 cm rim of air on the right. He is breathless. What is the next step?
options: High-flow oxygen only and observe for 2 weeks
Immediate chest drain under general anaesthesia
explanation: Symptomatic primary spontaneous pneumothorax: aspiration (or ambulatory device) first.

subject: PLB
body: A woman on the combined pill has pleuritic pain, tachycardia and a swollen calf. Wells score suggests PE is likely. What is the investigation of choice?
explanation: If PE is likely, arrange CTPA (and start interim anticoagulation if there will be a delay).

subject: PLB
body: Which spirometry result supports a diagnosis of COPD?
options: Normal FEV₁ with low DLCO only
explanation: Post-bronchodilator FEV₁/FVC <0.7 shows airflow obstruction.

subject: PLB
body: A patient with severe asthma has a silent chest, SpO₂ 90% and is exhausted. How is this classified?
explanation: Silent chest, cyanosis, exhaustion or SpO₂ <92% indicate life-threatening asthma.

subject: PLB
body: A COPD patient with known CO₂ retention is acutely unwell. What oxygen saturation target is appropriate?
explanation: Use controlled oxygen (e.g. Venturi mask) for those at risk of hypercapnic respiratory failure.

subject: PLB
body: A 60-year-old smoker has haemoptysis, weight loss and hypercalcaemia. Which lung cancer is most associated with hypercalcaemia (PTHrP)?
explanation: Small cell is associated with SIADH and ectopic ACTH.

subject: PLB
body: A former shipyard worker has pleural thickening, chest pain and a pleural effusion. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Asbestos exposure is the main risk factor.

subject: PLB
body: A 50-year-old with known alcohol excess vomits large amounts of fresh blood and is hypotensive. After resuscitation, which drug should be given before endoscopy if varices are suspected?
explanation: Suspected variceal bleed: terlipressin and antibiotics, then urgent endoscopy.

subject: PLB
body: A 25-year-old has bloody diarrhoea, urgency and continuous inflammation from the rectum on colonoscopy. What is the diagnosis?
explanation: UC starts in the rectum and extends continuously; Crohn's has skip lesions and can affect any part of the gut.

subject: PLB
body: Which serological test is first line for suspected coeliac disease (with adequate gluten intake)?
options: Tissue transglutaminase IgA with total IgA
explanation: Check total IgA to exclude IgA deficiency.

subject: PLB
body: Anti-mitochondrial antibodies in a middle-aged woman with itching and raised ALP suggest
explanation: PSC is associated with ulcerative colitis and pANCA.

subject: PLB
body: A 22-year-old has periumbilical pain moving to the right iliac fossa, fever and rebound tenderness. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Always do a pregnancy test in women of reproductive age with abdominal pain.

subject: PLB
body: A 45-year-old woman has right upper quadrant pain, fever and jaundice. What is this triad called?
explanation: Treat with antibiotics and biliary drainage (ERCP).

subject: PLB
body: A 70-year-old has colicky abdominal pain, distension, vomiting and absolute constipation. X-ray shows a 'coffee bean' sign. What is the diagnosis?
explanation: Often managed initially by flexible sigmoidoscopic decompression.

subject: PLB
body: Severe epigastric pain radiating to the back with raised serum amylase in a patient with gallstones suggests
explanation: Gallstones and alcohol are the most common causes.

subject: PLB
body: A 65-year-old smoker has a pulsatile, expansile abdominal mass and sudden back pain with hypotension. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Emergency vascular surgery.

subject: PLB
body: Which groin hernia lies below and lateral to the pubic tubercle and is more common in women?
explanation: Femoral hernias have a high risk of strangulation — repair urgently.

subject: PLB
body: A 60-year-old with iron-deficiency anaemia and weight loss is referred. Which cancer is most likely to present this way without obvious bleeding?
explanation: Right-sided tumours often present with occult bleeding and anaemia.

subject: PLB
body: A 19-year-old with type 1 diabetes has vomiting, glucose 28 mmol/L, ketones 5 mmol/L and pH 7.1. What is the first treatment priority?
explanation: DKA: fluids first, then fixed-rate IV insulin, with potassium replacement guided by levels.

subject: PLB
body: In DKA, fixed-rate IV insulin is given at what rate?
explanation: Continue long-acting basal insulin as well.

subject: PLB
body: Which is the first-line drug for most adults with type 2 diabetes?
explanation: Add an SGLT2 inhibitor where indicated (e.g. cardiovascular disease, heart failure).

subject: PLB
body: A woman has weight loss, tremor, heat intolerance, exophthalmos and a diffuse goitre. Which antibody is most likely raised?
explanation: Graves' disease; eye signs are specific to Graves'.

subject: PLB
body: A patient on long-term steroids is vomiting, hypotensive and has hyponatraemia and hyperkalaemia. What is the immediate treatment?
explanation: Adrenal crisis is an emergency.

subject: PLB
body: Hypercalcaemia with a raised (or inappropriately normal) PTH is most commonly caused by
explanation: Malignancy-related hypercalcaemia has a suppressed PTH.

subject: PLB
body: A patient has potassium 6.9 mmol/L with peaked T waves. What should be given FIRST?
explanation: Calcium stabilises the myocardium; then shift potassium with insulin–dextrose.

subject: PLB
body: Which finding defines stage 3 acute kidney injury (KDIGO)?
options: Creatinine rise of 26 µmol/L in 48 h
explanation: Stage 1 is a rise ≥26 µmol/L in 48 h or 1.5–1.9 × baseline.

subject: PLB
body: A child has periorbital oedema, heavy proteinuria and low albumin after a viral illness. What is the most likely cause?
explanation: Responds to steroids in most children.

subject: PLB
body: A 60-year-old has sudden right arm and face weakness and aphasia that started 90 minutes ago. CT shows no haemorrhage. What is the next treatment?
options: IV thrombolysis with alteplase (if no contraindications)
explanation: Thrombolysis within 4.5 hours; consider thrombectomy for large-vessel occlusion.

subject: PLB
body: A patient with TIA symptoms that have fully resolved should receive
options: Aspirin 300 mg immediately and specialist review within 24 hours
explanation: Unless contraindicated (e.g. on anticoagulants).

subject: PLB
body: A 35-year-old has a sudden 'worst ever' headache reaching maximum intensity within a minute. CT at 4 hours is normal. What is the most likely diagnosis to exclude?
explanation: CT within 6 hours is highly sensitive; if negative but suspicion high, lumbar puncture for xanthochromia per local guidance.

subject: PLB
body: A patient has been fitting for 5 minutes in the community. What is first-line treatment?
explanation: In hospital with IV access, give IV lorazepam.

subject: PLB
body: A young woman has painful loss of vision in one eye, worse with eye movement, and a previous episode of leg numbness. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: MRI brain and spinal cord.

subject: PLB
body: An elderly man has resting tremor, bradykinesia and rigidity. What is the diagnosis?
explanation: Essential tremor is postural and improves with alcohol.

subject: PLB
body: A 70-year-old woman has a new headache, scalp tenderness and jaw claudication. ESR is raised. What should be done immediately?
options: Wait for temporal artery biopsy results
explanation: Giant cell arteritis risks permanent visual loss; treat first.

subject: PLB
body: Glasgow Coma Scale: a patient opens eyes to pain, makes incomprehensible sounds and withdraws from pain. What is the GCS?

subject: PLB
body: A student has fever, headache, neck stiffness and a non-blanching rash. In the community, what should the GP do immediately?
options: Give IM/IV benzylpenicillin and arrange urgent transfer
Arrange a lumbar puncture in the surgery
explanation: Suspected meningococcal disease: give antibiotics without delay.

subject: PLB
body: A traveller returning from sub-Saharan Africa has fever and rigors. What investigation is essential?
options: Thick and thin blood films (or rapid antigen test) for malaria
explanation: Malaria must be excluded in any febrile returning traveller.

subject: PLB
body: Which is the standard initial treatment regimen for active pulmonary TB?
options: Rifampicin, isoniazid, pyrazinamide and ethambutol for 2 months, then rifampicin and isoniazid for 4 months
explanation: Give pyridoxine with isoniazid to prevent neuropathy.

subject: PLB
body: A patient has suspected sepsis. Which should be done within the first hour (Sepsis Six)?
options: Wait for culture results before antibiotics
Give IV antibiotics, take blood cultures, give oxygen if needed, measure lactate, give IV fluids, monitor urine output
explanation: Early antibiotics save lives.

subject: PLB
body: A woman has fatigue and a microcytic anaemia with low ferritin. What is the most likely cause?
options: Anaemia of chronic disease with high ferritin
explanation: Investigate the cause, e.g. menstrual or GI blood loss.

subject: PLB
body: Macrocytic anaemia with neuropathy and positive intrinsic factor antibodies suggests
explanation: Treat with IM hydroxocobalamin.

subject: PLB
body: A patient with sickle cell disease has severe pain in multiple limbs. What is the first-line management?
options: Prompt analgesia (often opioids), IV fluids and oxygen if hypoxic
explanation: Give analgesia within 30 minutes of arrival.

subject: PLB
body: Which blood test is used to monitor warfarin therapy?
explanation: Unfractionated heparin is monitored with APTT.

subject: PLB
body: Painless lymphadenopathy, night sweats and Reed–Sternberg cells on biopsy indicate
explanation: Pain in nodes after alcohol is a classic (rare) feature.

subject: PLB
body: A 6-month-old has coryza, cough, wheeze and fine crackles in December. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Supportive care; admit if poor feeding, apnoea or low SpO₂.

subject: PLB
body: A 2-year-old has a barking cough, inspiratory stridor and mild fever. What is first-line treatment?
options: A single dose of oral dexamethasone
explanation: Croup: steroids for all; nebulised adrenaline for severe cases.

subject: PLB
body: A 4-year-old has fever for 6 days, conjunctivitis, red lips, rash and swollen hands. What is the most important complication to screen for?
explanation: Kawasaki disease: treat with IV immunoglobulin and aspirin.

subject: PLB
body: A newborn has jaundice within the first 24 hours of life. What is the most important consideration?
options: It is pathological until proven otherwise — check bilirubin urgently
explanation: Consider haemolysis (e.g. rhesus or ABO incompatibility) or infection.

subject: PLB
body: Maintenance fluid for a 25 kg child using the Holliday–Segar method is
explanation: 100 mL/kg for the first 10 kg (1,000) + 50 mL/kg for the next 10 kg (500) + 20 mL/kg thereafter (100) = 1,600 mL/day.

subject: PLB
body: At what age does a child typically walk independently?
explanation: Not walking by 18 months warrants assessment.

subject: PLB
body: A 5-year-old has a limp and hip pain after a viral illness. He is well, afebrile and bears weight. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Fever, inability to weight-bear or raised inflammatory markers suggest septic arthritis.

subject: PLB
body: An overweight 13-year-old boy has knee pain and an externally rotated leg. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Hip pathology can present as knee pain.

subject: PLB
body: A woman 6 weeks after her last period has unilateral pelvic pain and light bleeding. Pregnancy test is positive. What must be excluded?
explanation: Arrange urgent transvaginal ultrasound.

subject: PLB
body: A woman at 34 weeks has BP 160/110, headache, visual disturbance and proteinuria. Which drug prevents seizures?
explanation: Severe pre-eclampsia: magnesium sulfate for seizure prophylaxis; labetalol/nifedipine for BP.

subject: PLB
body: Who should be offered aspirin 75–150 mg from 12 weeks of pregnancy?
options: Women at high risk of pre-eclampsia (e.g. chronic hypertension or previous pre-eclampsia)
explanation: Taken nightly until birth.

subject: PLB
body: Painless vaginal bleeding at 32 weeks with a non-tender uterus suggests
explanation: Avoid digital vaginal examination until praevia is excluded.

subject: PLB
body: Painful bleeding at 34 weeks with a tense, 'woody' uterus suggests
explanation: Bleeding may be concealed; maternal shock can be out of proportion to visible loss.

subject: PLB
body: A 28-year-old has irregular periods, acne, hirsutism and polycystic ovaries on ultrasound. What is the diagnosis?
explanation: Rotterdam criteria: 2 of oligo/anovulation, hyperandrogenism, polycystic ovaries.

subject: PLB
body: At what age does routine cervical screening start in England?
explanation: HPV primary screening.

subject: PLB
body: Postmenopausal bleeding in a 60-year-old woman requires
options: Urgent referral (suspected cancer pathway) for endometrial cancer
explanation: Transvaginal ultrasound is usually the first investigation.

subject: PLB
body: A patient with schizophrenia on clozapine has a sore throat and fever. What test is needed urgently?
explanation: Clozapine can cause life-threatening neutropenia.

subject: PLB
body: A patient on lithium has coarse tremor, vomiting, diarrhoea and confusion. What is the likely problem?
explanation: Stop lithium, check levels and renal function, give IV fluids.

subject: PLB
body: Which medication is first line for treating moderate depression in adults when a drug is indicated?
options: A tricyclic as first choice in all
explanation: Combine with psychological therapy.

subject: PLB
body: A patient has fever, rigidity, confusion and a very high CK after starting haloperidol. What is the diagnosis?
explanation: Stop the antipsychotic; supportive care.

subject: PLB
body: A patient on an SSRI and tramadol develops agitation, hyperreflexia, clonus and fever. What is the diagnosis?
explanation: Clonus and hyperreflexia are key features.

subject: PLB
body: Which treatment should be given to a patient with alcohol dependence at risk of Wernicke's encephalopathy?
explanation: Give thiamine before glucose.

subject: PLB
body: A 15-year-old asks for contraception and does not want her parents told. She understands the advice and is in a stable relationship. What should the doctor do?
options: Provide contraception if she is Fraser competent, while encouraging her to involve her parents
Tell her to come back at 16
explanation: Fraser guidelines apply; safeguarding concerns must still be considered.

subject: PLB
body: A patient with capacity refuses a life-saving blood transfusion for religious reasons. What should the doctor do?
options: Respect the refusal and document the discussion
explanation: A competent adult can refuse treatment even if it leads to death.

subject: PLB
body: Under the Mental Capacity Act, capacity is
options: assumed absent in all elderly patients
assumed unless proven otherwise and is decision-specific
explanation: A person must understand, retain, weigh and communicate the decision.

subject: PLB
body: A patient with epilepsy continues to drive after a seizure and refuses to inform the DVLA. What should the doctor do after trying to persuade them?
options: Inform the DVLA without telling the patient
Inform the DVLA and tell the patient you are doing so
explanation: GMC guidance allows disclosure in the public interest.

subject: PLB
body: A doctor makes an error that harms a patient. Under the professional duty of candour, the doctor should
options: Tell the patient, apologise, explain what happened and what will be done
explanation: Openness and honesty are required.

subject: PLB
body: Which statutory notifiable disease must a doctor report to the UK Health Security Agency?
explanation: Notification is required on clinical suspicion.

subject: PLB
body: A colleague smells of alcohol before a ward round. What should the doctor do first?
options: Report to the GMC first without telling anyone locally
Confront them in front of patients
Ensure patient safety by raising it with a senior colleague immediately
explanation: Patient safety comes first; escalate through the right channels.

subject: PLB
body: A patient on simvastatin starts clarithromycin. What is the main risk?
explanation: Clarithromycin inhibits CYP3A4; withhold the statin during the course.

subject: PLB
body: A patient on warfarin is prescribed a course of clarithromycin. What may happen?
explanation: Monitor INR closely.

subject: PLB
body: Which drug should be withheld before iodinated contrast in a patient with reduced kidney function, per local guidance?
explanation: Risk of lactic acidosis if contrast-induced AKI occurs.

subject: PLB
body: A patient taking an ACE inhibitor and spironolactone is at particular risk of
explanation: Monitor potassium and renal function.

subject: PLB
body: Which antibiotic should be avoided in pregnancy because it affects fetal teeth and bones?
explanation: Tetracyclines are contraindicated in pregnancy and in children under 12.

subject: PLB
body: A patient with opioid overdose has pinpoint pupils and RR 6/min. What is the treatment?
explanation: Repeat doses may be needed as naloxone is short-acting.

subject: PLB
body: Paracetamol overdose: which treatment is given when the level is above the treatment line?
explanation: Staggered or uncertain-time overdoses are treated regardless of level.

subject: PLB
body: A changing pigmented lesion with irregular borders, multiple colours and diameter over 6 mm should be
options: Referred urgently on the suspected cancer pathway for melanoma
explanation: Use the 7-point checklist or ABCDE.

subject: PLB
body: A pearly nodule with rolled edges and telangiectasia on the nose of an older man is most likely
explanation: Locally invasive, rarely metastasises.

subject: PLB
body: A 65-year-old has a painful red eye, halos around lights, vomiting and a fixed mid-dilated pupil. What is the diagnosis?
explanation: Emergency: refer urgently; treatments lower intraocular pressure.

subject: PLB
body: Sudden painless loss of vision with a cherry-red spot at the macula indicates
explanation: Vein occlusion shows a 'stormy sunset' of haemorrhages.

subject: PLB
body: A patient has sudden unilateral sensorineural hearing loss. What is the appropriate action?
options: Urgent ENT referral (same day or within 24 hours)
explanation: Early steroids may improve outcome; exclude other causes.

subject: PLB
body: A 45-year-old woman has symmetrical small-joint polyarthritis with morning stiffness over 1 hour. Which antibody is most specific?
explanation: Start a DMARD such as methotrexate early.

subject: PLB
body: A man has a sudden hot, swollen first metatarsophalangeal joint after a heavy night of drinking. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Needle-shaped negatively birefringent crystals on aspiration.

subject: PLB
body: When should allopurinol usually be started for recurrent gout?
options: After the acute attack has settled (often with colchicine cover)
Only if uric acid is normal
During the acute attack as first treatment
explanation: Starting during an attack can prolong it; many clinicians now start once settled.

subject: PLB
body: An elderly woman falls and has a shortened, externally rotated leg. What is the most likely injury?
explanation: Posterior hip dislocation classically gives a shortened, internally rotated leg.

subject: PLB
body: A patient after a tibial fracture has pain out of proportion, worse on passive stretch. What is the concern?
explanation: Emergency fasciotomy may be needed.

subject: PLB
body: A patient has anaphylaxis with wheeze and hypotension. What is the first drug?
explanation: Repeat after 5 minutes if no improvement.

subject: PLB
body: In adult cardiac arrest with a shockable rhythm, when is adrenaline first given?
explanation: Then every 3–5 minutes; amiodarone 300 mg after the third shock.

subject: PLB
body: A patient with stable angina needs short-term symptom relief. What should be prescribed with a beta-blocker or CCB?
explanation: Also offer aspirin and a statin for secondary prevention.

subject: PLB
body: Which drug should be given to all patients with acute coronary syndrome unless contraindicated?
explanation: Then a second antiplatelet per local protocol.

subject: PLB
body: A 25-year-old has palpitations and an ECG with a short PR interval and delta waves. What is the diagnosis?
explanation: An accessory pathway; avoid AV-node blockers if AF develops.

subject: PLB
body: Which statin is offered for primary prevention when 10-year QRISK3 is 10% or more?
explanation: Atorvastatin 80 mg is used for secondary prevention.

subject: PLB
body: A 30-year-old with uncontrolled asthma on a low-dose ICS inhaler. What is the usual next step in current UK guidance?
options: Switch to an ICS/formoterol combination (MART) or add a long-acting beta-agonist per local pathway
explanation: Check adherence and inhaler technique first.

subject: PLB
body: A patient with sarcoidosis classically has which chest X-ray finding?
explanation: Also raised ACE and hypercalcaemia.

subject: PLB
body: Obstructive sleep apnoea is screened with which questionnaire?
explanation: Confirm with sleep studies.

subject: PLB
body: A patient with dyspepsia and positive H. pylori test should receive
options: Triple therapy: a PPI with two antibiotics for 7 days
explanation: Common regimen: PPI + amoxicillin + clarithromycin (or metronidazole).

subject: PLB
body: Which is a red flag needing urgent endoscopy referral in a patient with dyspepsia?
explanation: Also age ≥55 with weight loss and dyspepsia.

subject: PLB
body: Paracentesis in a patient with cirrhotic ascites shows a neutrophil count of 400 cells/mm³. What is the diagnosis?
explanation: Neutrophils >250/mm³; treat with IV antibiotics.

subject: PLB
body: A patient with cirrhosis is confused with a flapping tremor. What is first-line treatment?
explanation: Look for and treat precipitants (infection, bleeding, constipation).

subject: PLB
body: A 50-year-old has left iliac fossa pain, fever and raised inflammatory markers. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: CT abdomen confirms complications such as abscess.

subject: PLB
body: A 20-year-old has sudden severe testicular pain, a high-riding testis and absent cremasteric reflex. What is the management?
explanation: Testicular torsion: surgery within 6 hours to save the testis.

subject: PLB
body: Which investigation is first line for suspected renal colic in most adults?
explanation: Ultrasound is preferred in pregnancy and children.

subject: PLB
body: A breast lump in a 30-year-old woman should be assessed with
options: Triple assessment: clinical exam, imaging and biopsy
explanation: Ultrasound is the imaging of choice under 35–40.

subject: PLB
body: A patient has low TSH and high free T4. Which is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: High TSH with low T4 = primary hypothyroidism.

subject: PLB
body: HbA1c diagnostic of diabetes is
explanation: 42–47 indicates non-diabetic hyperglycaemia.

subject: PLB
body: A patient with type 2 diabetes is hypoglycaemic and drowsy but can swallow. What is first?
options: 15–20 g of fast-acting carbohydrate such as glucose tablets or juice
explanation: Recheck glucose after 10–15 minutes.

subject: PLB
body: Hyponatraemia with low serum osmolality and concentrated urine in a euvolaemic patient with small cell lung cancer suggests
explanation: Treat with fluid restriction initially.

subject: PLB
body: A woman has unilateral throbbing headaches with nausea and photophobia lasting 12 hours, with visual zigzags beforehand. What is first-line acute treatment?
options: A triptan with an NSAID or paracetamol
explanation: Avoid combined hormonal contraception in migraine with aura.

subject: PLB
body: A man has excruciating unilateral periorbital headaches with tearing, occurring daily for weeks. What is the acute treatment?
explanation: Verapamil is used for prevention.

subject: PLB
body: Facial weakness that spares the forehead suggests
options: An upper motor neurone lesion such as a stroke
explanation: Bell's palsy (LMN) affects the forehead too.

subject: PLB
body: Back pain with saddle anaesthesia and urinary retention suggests
explanation: Surgical emergency.

subject: PLB
body: A sexually active man has urethral discharge and dysuria. Gram-negative intracellular diplococci are seen. What is the treatment?
explanation: Gonorrhoea; test for other STIs and arrange partner notification.

subject: PLB
body: Uncomplicated lower UTI in a non-pregnant woman is usually treated with
options: Nitrofurantoin (if eGFR allows) or trimethoprim for 3 days
explanation: Follow local resistance guidance.

subject: PLB
body: A child has a vesicular rash in crops at different stages and is mildly unwell. What is the diagnosis?
explanation: Avoid NSAIDs; keep away from pregnant women and the immunosuppressed.

subject: PLB
body: A child has a sore throat, strawberry tongue and a sandpaper-like rash. What is the treatment?
explanation: Scarlet fever is notifiable in England.

subject: PLB
body: A patient on heparin has a platelet fall of over 50% at day 7. What should be suspected?
explanation: Stop heparin and use a non-heparin anticoagulant.

subject: PLB
body: A patient with bone pain, anaemia, hypercalcaemia and renal impairment most likely has
explanation: CRAB features; check serum protein electrophoresis and free light chains.

subject: PLB
body: A 3-week-old boy has projectile non-bilious vomiting after feeds and is hungry. What is the diagnosis?
explanation: Hypochloraemic hypokalaemic metabolic alkalosis; pyloromyotomy.

subject: PLB
body: A 9-month-old has episodic colicky pain, drawing up the legs, and redcurrant jelly stools. What is the diagnosis?
explanation: Ultrasound shows a target sign; air enema reduction.

subject: PLB
body: Bilious vomiting in a newborn is
options: a surgical emergency until proven otherwise (e.g. malrotation)
explanation: Urgent surgical review.

subject: PLB
body: A febrile child under 3 months with temperature 38 °C or higher should be
options: Considered high risk and assessed urgently in hospital
explanation: NICE traffic-light: a red feature.

subject: PLB
body: A woman has amenorrhoea, a positive pregnancy test and heavy bleeding with an open cervical os. What type of miscarriage is this?
explanation: Threatened = closed os with a viable pregnancy.

subject: PLB
body: Rhesus-negative women are given anti-D to prevent
options: haemolytic disease of the newborn in future pregnancies
explanation: Given routinely and after sensitising events.

subject: PLB
body: Which test is used to screen for gestational diabetes in at-risk women?
options: 75 g oral glucose tolerance test at 24–28 weeks
explanation: Earlier OGTT if previous gestational diabetes.

subject: PLB
body: A woman has cyclical pelvic pain, dysmenorrhoea, deep dyspareunia and subfertility. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Laparoscopy is the diagnostic gold standard.

subject: PLB
body: Which tool is used to screen for alcohol misuse?
explanation: The Edinburgh scale screens for postnatal depression.

subject: PLB
